rounds.text: Gujarat Terce Laboratories Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E ratio of just 11.5x [E1]. This attractive valuation is paired with exceptional operational profitability, highlighted by a stellar Return on Equity of 30.2% [E13] and a robust Return on Assets of 8.47% [E8]. These profitability metrics heavily outperform sector benchmarks, where the average ROE stands at a much lower 10.34% and ROA at 5.74% [E8, E9]. Furthermore, recent performance demonstrates a decisive upward inflection in capital efficiency, evidenced by a median return on equity of 30% over the last year [E29] and matching screen signals [E62]. Conceded: the company has a low historical median return on equity of -1% over 10 years [E26] and 2% over 5 years [E27], alongside a zero dividend yield [E4].

The recent high return on equity of 30.2% [E13] masks a severely troubled historical track record, highlighted by a 10-year median return on equity of -1% [E26] and a 5-year median of just 2% [E27]. This structural lack of sustained profitability is further underscored by a low 3-year median return on equity of 8% [E28] and an official company flag noting a low return on equity of 7.77% over the last three years [E57]. Investors receive no cash return for bearing this volatility, as the dividend yield sits entirely at 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, the stock languishes near the bottom of its historical spectrum, sitting only 23% of the way up its 52-week range between a low of 29 and a high of 60 [E5]. Conceded: the business achieves a strong ROA of 8.47% against a sector benchmark of 5.74% [E8] and a short-term ROE of 25.62% to 30.2% [E9, E13].

Conceded: the company displays a recent ROE of 30.2% [E13] and an ROA of 8.47% [E8]. However, treating this single-year surge as structural profitability ignores the devastating multi-year reality: the median return on equity is a dismal -1% over 10 years [E26] and a meager 2% over 5 years [E27]. Even over a compressed 3-year horizon, the median ROE is only 8% [E28], and filed statements explicitly flag a low 3-year return on equity of 7.77% as a negative indicator [E57]. The bull's reliance on a transient 30% ROE [E29, E62] is wholly unsupported by the company's long-term historical track record. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero return in cash while waiting for this cyclical volatility to stabilize, as evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Finally, the stock trades at 23% of the way up its 52-year range [E5], showing that the market rightly refuses to price this erratic earnings profile at a premium.
